rows.location: course/modules/AC/AC2/L05.html E2 solution (cause of -2.7937 vs -2.7996)
rows.evidence: Round 3: L05.html E2 solution now says 'The cause is the finite sort: each month sorts 500 firms ... The lab prints the realised gap at two firm counts ... two counts are not enough to establish the rate.' The printed numbers (-2.7912 at 500 and -2.7991 at 5,000, 20 seeds each; -2.7937 at 500 over 200 seeds; analytic -2.79962) show that the gap moves toward the analytic value as the sort grows, and they are consistent with a finite-sort cause. They do not establish that the finite sort is the cause: the page prints no sweep, and the analytic value is a population quantity whose gap at a finite n is not checked by any printed line. My own 400-seed sweep (recompute_l05_r3.py, not printed by the lab) gives gaps -2.7421 (n=50), -2.7705 (n=100), -2.7938 (n=500), -2.7990 (n=5000), i.e. bias about -2.9/n, which supports the cause but is not on the page. The 20-seed and 200-seed means at 500 firms differ by 0.0025 with SE 0.0018 (seed variation, consistent). Required fix: cite a printed sweep or write 'consistent with a finite-sort effect'.
rows.fix: Cite a printed sweep over firm counts (50, 100, 500, 5000) in Lab 1, or soften 'The cause is' to 'consistent with a finite-sort effect'.

rows.location: course/modules/AC/AC2/L06.html Lab 1 interpretation ('conditional-mean prediction for a1 is 0.6223')
rows.evidence: Round 3 re-verified: E[d|X] = SHIFT x P(manipulator|X) = 0.05 x 0.10 = 0.005 (constant: manipulators are a uniform permutation independent of X). Prop 3.3 applied to d' = E[d|X] gives (X'X)^-1 X' (0.005*1) = 0.6223 for a1 (analytic, recomputed). Monte Carlo with X fixed at seed 606, 4,000 redraws of manipulators and noise: E[a1_all - a1_nm | X] = 0.6295 (SE 0.0065) and E[a1_all - C | X] = 0.6290 (SE 0.0077), both consistent with 0.6223; sd of the difference 0.4125, so the realised 0.2084 is one draw. The page's 'a different quantity from the realised 0.2084, which is one draw' is supported. The page does not say which quantity 0.6223 predicts; it is the conditional mean of the difference (equivalently of the all-firm bias relative to 0.05 because the non-manipulator estimator has conditional mean C).

rows.location: course/modules/AC/AC2/L06.html 'Stated before running' hypothesis paragraph (Lab 1 hypothesis)
rows.evidence: The hypothesis (stated before running) says: 'Estimated on all firms, the coefficients should shift by the realised projection of the planted term, which the lab decomposes.' The lab's own decomposition (recomputed, identity residual 1e-14) shows the all-minus-non-manipulator shift is 0.2084 = 0.1425 (projection of the planted term) + 0.1965 (all-firm noise projection) - 0.1306 (non-manipulator deviation). The shift is therefore not the projection of the planted term alone, and the sentence contradicts the decomposition on the same page. Required fix: 'should shift by the projection of the planted term plus sampling noise'.
rows.fix: Replace 'should shift by the realised projection of the planted term' with 'should shift by the projection of the planted term plus sampling noise'.

rows.location: course/modules/AC/AC2/L06.html §2, paragraph after Definition 2.1, first sentence
rows.evidence: 'The model adds a receivables adjustment to the revenue term: it uses the change in revenue less the change in receivables, so that revenue booked as receivables is not counted as normal growth.' The 'so that' clause states the purpose (the rationale) of the adjustment with no grade, key or locator, and the same paragraph then says 'The rationale for the receivables term is not sourced in this lesson'. The formula's arithmetic effect is verified (ΔREV - ΔREC enters the regressor); the purpose clause is not. Required fix: describe the mechanical effect only.
rows.fix: Delete the 'so that ... not counted as normal growth' purpose clause; keep the mechanical description and the not-sourced disclaimer.

rows.location: course/modules/AC/AC2/L06.html §5 bullet 'The receivables adjustment assumes the manipulation runs through revenue.'
rows.evidence: The bullet now says the adjustment 'matters only if the manipulation runs through revenue'. Nothing in the lesson, the registry abstract of dechow1995detecting, or Lab 1 supports a 'matters only if' condition: the regressor (ΔREV - ΔREC)/A enters the fit whether or not the manipulation is in revenue, and Lab 1 plants the manipulation in the discretionary term, which the lab itself does not test against any channel. The claim is the same unsourced rationale the §2 disclaimer says is not sourced. Required fix: state the design fact (the adjustment is a regressor; Lab 1 has no revenue channel) and drop 'matters only if'.
rows.fix: Drop 'matters only if the manipulation runs through revenue'; state only that Lab 1 has no revenue channel.
